x: The Kavi Club was at Kumudavalli (West Godavari) in 1897. The traps: the 1882 Brahmo Samaj was at Machilipatnam (Guntur's Samaj came in 1898), the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam at Hyderabad dates to 1901, and the Kakinada Samaj was at Kakinada in 1888.

Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu founded the Brahmo Samaj at Machilipatnam in 1882. The Kakinada Samaj (1888) was founded by Tayi Surya Prakasarao Naidu, the Guntur Samaj (1898) by Pillarisetty Sitaramayya, and the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj (1878) by Veeresalingam.
Kanyasulkam is dated 1892 (written in 1890 and first staged on 13 August 1892) and was revised in 1909, when its second edition was dedicated to Ananda Gajapati.

Gurajada's line means that a country is its people, not merely its soil. ⚠ Sources differ on the poem it comes from: Desamunu Preminchumanna / Desabhakti in most notes, while the APPSC 2025 key says Kanyaka.

The first widow remarriage in Andhra was in 1881, Stree Samajam at Brundavanapuram and Hindu Sundari both date to 1902, and the Andhra Desa Library Association to 1914. Since B and C share the year 1902, the key places Stree Samajam before Hindu Sundari, giving D, B, C, A; option C (D, C, B, A) differs only in that tie.

A Memorandum of Modern Telugu Prose is Gidugu Ramamurthy's work. Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini was Kokkonda Venkataratnam's orthodox journal, The Vicar of Wakefield (Goldsmith) was the model for Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitra, and Desabhakti is linked with Gurajada.

Vartamana Tarangini (8 June 1842) was Sayyad Rahamtulla's journal. Rajasekhara Charitram was Veeresalingam's novel, Satyaduta came from the Bellary Christian Mission, and Seesari Charitra was by Vavilala (Ponnekanti Telaganaryudu wrote Yayati Charitra).

C.P. Brown compiled the Telugu-English and English-Telugu dictionaries of 1853. Colin Mackenzie was the first Surveyor General (1815), William Carey produced the complete Telugu Bible at Serampore, and Thomas Munro kept Telugu as an administrative language rather than replacing it.
The phrase 'Italian of the East' was first used by Nicolo de Conti; C.P. Brown later applied it to Telugu, which is why Brown is the trap.
Vidyasagar performed the first widow remarriage in Bengal on 7 December 1856. 11 December 1881 is the date of Andhra's first widow remarriage at Rajahmundry, so the options mix the two events' dates.

Deva Samaj — Shiv Narayan Agnihotri; Seva Samiti — Hriday Nath Kunzru (Allahabad, 1914); Social Service League — N.M. Joshi (Bombay, 1911); Sharada Sadan — Pandita Ramabai (1889). Note the APPSC-G2 2023 key paired Deva Samaj with Radhakant Deb, though standard texts give it to Agnihotri.

The age of consent is 18 under POCSO/BNS, while the minimum marriage age under the PCMA 2006 is 18 for women and 21 for men. Option C states the same figures but omits the laws; A is the complete statement of the distinction and is the key.

Vivekavardhani was started by Veeresalingam in 1874. The Bengalee was Surendranath Banerjee's paper (1879), Kesari was Tilak's, and Swadesamitran was founded by G. Subramania Iyer (1882); Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika in 1908.
